stories.title: Jewish, Muslim voters see communities under attack this election
stories.summary: An event in Canton hosted Democratic women, including Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib, who expressed concerns about rising anti-Muslim sentiment and hate speech impacting their children. Separately, a group of rabbis called for more measured language in Michigan's U.S. Senate race, accusing a progressive PAC of using anti-Jewish stereotypes in an ad.

photo.alt: Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib speaking at a Democratic event in Canton on October 27, 2026.

inputFacts.title: Jewish, Muslim voters see communities under attack this election
inputFacts.summary: Members of Michigan’s Jewish and Muslim communities express concerns about rising hate speech and attack ads during the 2026 U.S. Senate election. Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed faces criticism for being associated with a political ad using 9/11 imagery, while rabbis accuse progressive groups of antisemitic rhetoric. Events in Canton and Southfield highlighted fears of dehumanization and calls for politicians to address extremism within their parties.

stories.title: State funding advances Arbor South development, expands local business opportunities
stories.summary: The Arbor South mixed-use development in Ann Arbor, approved by Washtenaw County in May, secured state Act 381 tax increment financing to support its construction starting January. The project aims to provide affordable housing and commercial space on a 20-acre brownfield site, with developers receiving repayment through future tax revenue.

photo.alt: An aerial view of Ann Arbor

inputFacts.title: State funding advances Arbor South development, expands local business opportunities
inputFacts.summary: State funding from the Michigan State Housing Development Authority (MSF) has advanced the Arbor South development project in Ann Arbor, aiming to address housing affordability and support local businesses. The project includes affordable housing, commercial spaces, and preservation of existing businesses like Shawarma Shop. Developers emphasize the importance of state support in navigating high construction costs and aligning with Governor Whitmer's administration goals.

stories.title: Beyond the books: How Toyota and the Ypsi District Library are opening doors to STEM
stories.summary: The Ypsilanti District Library's Project STEM@YDL, supported by Toyota, has expanded STEM access for children and families since spring 2023. The initiative provides educational equipment, programming, and connections to STEM professionals, with 176 programs attended by 4,879 people in 2025, fostering problem-solving and career exploration.

photo.alt: Kids celebrating CRISPR Day with a DNA extraction experiment using gatorade and saliva at the YDL Whittaker branch. Photo by Doug Coombe.

inputFacts.title: Beyond the books: How Toyota and the Ypsi District Library are opening doors to STEM
inputFacts.summary: Toyota has provided $30,000 annually since 2023 to the Ypsilanti District Library (YDL) to expand STEM programming, purchase educational equipment, and connect young people with STEM professionals. The partnership supports Project STEM@YDL, which offers hands-on learning opportunities, collaborates with external organizations, and has reached thousands of participants through workshops, play spaces, and community events. The initiative aims to create pathways from kindergarten to careers in high-growth industries while fostering community engagement through discovery and innovation.

inputFacts.title: CSG takes part in SAPAC workshop
inputFacts.summary: The College Student Government (CSG) participated in a workshop organized by the Student Affairs Policy and Advocacy Committee (SAPAC). The event focused on student government collaboration and policy development.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor considers changes to food truck parking rules
inputFacts.summary: Ann Arbor may revise its food truck ordinance to eliminate a requirement that locations hosting two food trucks must have at least 20 off-street parking spaces. The current rule, which differs from other city permits, will be updated to align with peer communities' practices. The City Planning Commission discussed the potential change during a workshop on October 23, 2026.

inputFacts.title: Republicans distort rape case to falsely attack Christina Hines
inputFacts.summary: A forensic investigation into allegations that Smith raped Fields in 2026 found no evidence to substantiate the claims, leading prosecutors to dismiss the case. Despite this, Republican campaigns have used the case to attack Christina Hines, who previously prosecuted over 100 serious crimes. Hines' opponent, Michael Bouchard Jr., has also faced scrutiny over political ties and campaign donations.

inputFacts.title: 'Is my son really safe?': Taylor High School brawls prompt parent concerns
inputFacts.summary: Four students were arrested following two separate fights at Taylor High School on Monday and Tuesday, according to police. Videos of the fights circulated on social media, showing large groups of students joining the altercations and raising concerns about school safety. Parents are demanding answers after the incidents, which also involved the discovery of four illegally possessed weapons, including an automatic weapon, during a separate police encounter.

inputFacts.title: Ypsilanti Community Schools upgrading emergency alert system
inputFacts.summary: Ypsilanti Community Schools is rolling out the Centegix Crisis Alert system to replace the aging EPIC SAFE Alerts. The new system uses wearable badges that staff can activate by pressing a button three times to send emergency alerts or initiate facility-wide lockdowns. Technology Director Solomon Zheng highlighted the system's expanded range, covering areas from the high school to RCTC.

inputFacts.title: Taylor police: Multiple arrested, more suspended after back-to-back fights at Taylor High School
inputFacts.summary: Taylor police arrested five students following two fights at Taylor High School, with two male students and three men later released. Three men were arrested with four illegally possessed weapons, including an automatic weapon. At least 11 students were suspended, and school officials urged parents to prevent further conflicts.

inputFacts.summary: The LSA Opportunity Hub marked its 10th anniversary as a key resource for students seeking career guidance and professional development opportunities within the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts.

inputFacts.title: Students Organize for Syria hosts ‘Psychiatry in Syria’
inputFacts.summary: Students Organize for Syria hosted a panel discussion on the psychological impact of conflict and displacement on Syrian communities at the University of Michigan. The event, held in collaboration with The Muslim Coalition and Wolverine Shifa, featured experts discussing trauma, cultural stigma around mental health, and strategies for support. Panelists emphasized the long-term effects of war trauma and the importance of culturally relevant mental health approaches.
